concepts.def: The system of receptors, neurones and the central nervous system that enables humans to react to their surroundings and to coordinate their behaviour.
A cell or structure that detects a stimulus, for example the light receptors in the retina or the temperature receptors in the skin.
A nerve cell that carries information as electrical impulses from receptors to the central nervous system, and from the central nervous system to effectors.
The brain and spinal cord. The CNS coordinates the response of effectors to the information it receives from receptors.
A structure that brings about the response. Effectors may be muscles contracting or glands secreting hormones.
The sequence stimulus → receptor → coordinator → effector → response, which describes how the body detects and responds to a change.
An automatic and rapid response to a stimulus that does not involve the conscious part of the brain.
The pathway taken by an impulse in a reflex action: receptor → sensory neurone → relay neurone in the CNS → motor neurone → effector.
The junction between two neurones. A chemical is released and diffuses across the gap, setting off a new electrical impulse in the next neurone.

mcqs.q: A single neurone carries impulses from a receptor in the toe to the spinal cord. Which statement best explains how this structure is adapted to its function?
options: It is long, so impulses reach the CNS quickly.
It detects the stimulus and causes the response.
It is part of the central nervous system.
It carries the impulse without using the CNS.
mcqs.explain: Information from receptors passes along cells (neurones) as electrical impulses to the central nervous system, so one long cell carries the impulse the whole way to the spinal cord without delay.

mcqs.q: Effectors in the human body may be:
options: muscles contracting or glands secreting
receptors detecting light and sound levels
skeletal muscles moving bones at a joint
sense organs that detect and respond
mcqs.explain: The CNS coordinates the response of effectors, which may be muscles contracting or glands secreting hormones.

mcqs.q: In a reflex arc, what is the function of the relay neurone?
options: It carries the impulse to the conscious brain.
It links the sensory neurone to the motor neurone in the CNS.
It carries the electrical impulse across the synapse.
It carries the impulse to the effector without the CNS.
mcqs.explain: In a reflex arc the sensory neurone passes the impulse across a synapse to a relay neurone in the CNS, which passes it on to the motor neurone that carries the impulse to the effector.

mcqs.q: Why is a reflex action important when a person touches a very hot object?
options: It gives the person time to decide how to act.
It keeps the impulse out of the nervous system.
It is rapid and automatic, reducing injury.
It lets the receptor produce the response itself.
mcqs.explain: Reflex actions are automatic and rapid; the hand is moved away from the stimulus before the conscious part of the brain is involved, which limits the damage done.

mcqs.q: A table shows one student's mean reaction time in three trials: trial 1, 0.28 s; trial 2, 0.24 s; trial 3, 0.21 s. What do these data show?
options: The reaction time fell across the trials.
The reaction time rose across all the trials.
The student reacted more slowly each time.
The results apply to other students too.
mcqs.explain: Reading the values in order from the table shows a decrease from 0.28 s to 0.21 s, which is the pattern the data support.

mcqs.q: Four students have mean reaction times of 0.15 s, 0.22 s, 0.28 s and 0.31 s. These values are drawn as a bar chart. Which statement about the chart is correct?
options: The tallest bar is the fastest time.
The shortest bar is the slowest time.
The tallest bar shows the 0.31 s time.
Each bar stands for the group as a whole.
mcqs.explain: Translating the numbers into graphical form, bar height is proportional to reaction time, so the largest value, 0.31 s, gives the tallest bar.
